newsitem.title: USA: AOL reaches pact in class action lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: AOL reaches pact in class action lawsuit.

text.p: America Online Inc. said it reached a preliminary agreement Thursday in a nationally certified class action lawsuit that was filed against it due to recent problems subscribers had in logging on to the network.
America Online said that as part of its agreement, it will expand its refund and credit policy to cover subscribers who had difficulty connecting to the service in February and March.

America Online was besieged by complaints about network access problems after the company switched to offering customers unlimited access for a flat rate of $19.95 a month on Dec. 1. Many members were so frustrated at not being able to sign on, or by difficulties in signing on, that they filed lawsuits against America Online.

The agreement provides refunds and credits upon written requests based on use for members who were online between two and 15 hours and experienced difficulty in connecting to America Online in either February or March.
The company did not specify any costs for the resolution of the nationwide class action, which was consolidated under one class in Circuit Court of Cook County, Ill.

But a spokeswoman said that America Online believes the $24 million charge it took against second quarter earnings to pay for its refund settlement with the 36 state attorneys general in January will cover these refunds and credits for all members.
"We really see that the statement allows us to close the chapter on the access problem," an America Online spokeswoman said.
The class action was certified in Illinois because plaintiff Steven Schwab, an America Online subscriber, filed the first class action suit against America Online in Cook County.
Any America Online member can either remain as part of the class or they can opt out of the settlement.

"This does really move us beyond the access issue," the America Online spokeswoman said. "We are really making significant progress. We have put 75,000 modems in since Jan. 1 and that has helped us have over 2.5 million more daily sessions."
